question.question: Will the Federal Reserve lower the upper bound of its federal funds target range at the October 27-28, 2026 FOMC meeting?
question.description: YES if the upper bound announced in the October 28 FOMC statement is lower than the upper bound immediately before that meeting; NO otherwise. Meeting calendar: https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm

params.question_origin: Author-written question using the official FOMC calendar

agents.rationale: Based on evidence from https://www.cnbc.com/2026/09/16/fed-rate-decision-september-2026.html, the Fed hiked rates to 3.75%-4% at the September 2026 meeting, with 16 of 18 participants expecting another rate hike later in 2026. From https://streetstats.finance/rates/fedfunds, futures markets as of late September 2026 are pricing the rate to rise to ~4.2% by December 2026, indicating further tightening expected. The September 2026 FOMC projections (https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomcprojtabl20260916.htm) show a median federal funds rate of 4.1% for end-2026, consistent with one more hike. All signals point to continued tightening, making a rate cut (lower upper bound) at the October 27-28 meeting extremely unlikely. Probability of YES is approximately 7%.

results.title: September Fed Meeting: Updates and Commentary | Kiplinger
results.snippet:
In June, the Fed's dot plot indicated expectations that the federal funds rate would be raised to 3.8% by the end of 2026 — suggesting one quarter-point rate hike this year.

But following several data points — including the August CPI report — that showed inflation remains well above the Fed's target, futures traders are pricing in two quarter-point rate increases by year's end. [...] The committee's economic projections show slightly higher GDP and inflation rates than what we saw in June. The FOMC also expects two additional rate hikes: one more this year, and one in 2027, before the federal funds rate starts coming down with an expected decline in inflation.

In the long run, the committee expects the federal funds rate to be between 3.0% and 4.0%, with PCE inflation reaching 2.0% by 2029. In June, the FOMC expected PCE to fall to 2.0% by 2028.

- David Payne [...] The strategist also thinks the median in the Summary of Economic Projections will forecast one additional rate hike this year and none in 2027.

- Karee Venema

## The Fed hikes rates for the first time since 2023

In a unanimous decision, the Federal Reserve voted to raise the federal funds rate by a quarter percentage point, as expected.

results.title: Fed rate decision September 2026: Rates rise to 3.75%-4%
results.snippet:
The Federal Reserve on Wednesday approved its first interest rate hike in more than three years and indicated another is to come, as part of an effort aimed at combating inflation brought on by spiraling oil prices and other factors.

In a move that markets widely anticipated, the central bank's Federal Open Market Committee voted 12-0 to increase its key interest rate by a quarter percentage point, or 25 basis points. The move brought the overnight funds rate to a target range of 3.75%-4%. [...] Updated projections the committee released Wednesday showed that a strong majority of officials think another hike is possible later this year.

The dot-plot grid of individual officials' expectations indicated that 16 of the 18 participants – Warsh has chosen not to submit a dot since taking the position – expected another rate increase, with four of those seeing two more as possible. Two participants expected the committee to stop at one hike. [...] "All three of those things lend themselves to a firm unanimous decision today," he said.

Despite a raft of conflicting recent statements from policymakers, markets had priced in a better than 90% chance that the FOMC would approve the increase, though there was chatter about the possibility of multiple dissents.

Persistently high inflation readings coupled with statements from Warsh a few weeks ago had convinced Wall Street that the Fed would OK its first rate increase since July 2023.

results.snippet:
The eight scheduled 2026 FOMC meetings are January 27–28; March 17–18; April 28–29; June 16–17; July 28–29; September 15–16; October 27–28; and December 8–9. The March, June, September, and December meetings include the Summary of Economic Projections (SEP).

### What time does the FOMC announce its decision? [...] The Federal Open Market Committee is the Federal Reserve body responsible for open market operations and the target range for the federal funds rate.

### Which 2026 FOMC meetings include the dot plot?

The March, June, September, and December 2026 meetings include the Summary of Economic Projections and its federal funds rate projections, commonly called the dot plot.

### How can an FOMC decision affect borrowing costs? [...] The FOMC directly sets the target range for the federal funds rate, not consumer loan rates. Its decisions and guidance can still influence Treasury yields, bank funding costs, mortgage rates, savings rates, and other borrowing costs, but those rates do not always move one-for-one with the Fed.

1. September Fed Meeting: Updates and Commentary | Kiplinger
   URL: https://www.kiplinger.com/investing/live/fed-meeting-updates-and-commentary-september-2026
   In June, the Fed's dot plot indicated expectations that the federal funds rate would be raised to 3.8% by the end of 2026 — suggesting one quarter-point rate hike this year.

But following several data points — including the August CPI report — that showed inflation remains well above the Fed's target, futures traders are pricing in two quarter-point rate increases by year's end. [...] The committee's economic projections show slightly higher GDP and inflation rates than what we saw in June. The FOMC also expects two additional rate hikes: one more this year, and one in 2027, before the federal funds rate starts coming down with an expected decline in inflation.

In the long run, the committee expects the federal funds rate to be between 3.0% and 4.0%, with PCE inflation reaching 2.0% by 2029. In June, the FOMC expected PCE to fall to 2.0% by 2028.

- David Payne [...] The strategist also thinks the median in the Summary of Economic Projections will forecast one additional rate hike this year and none in 2027.

- Karee Venema

## The Fed hikes rates for the first time since 2023

In a unanimous decision, the Federal Reserve voted to raise the federal funds rate by a quarter percentage point, as expected.

2. Fed rate decision September 2026: Rates rise to 3.75%-4%
   URL: https://www.cnbc.com/2026/09/16/fed-rate-decision-september-2026.html
   The Federal Reserve on Wednesday approved its first interest rate hike in more than three years and indicated another is to come, as part of an effort aimed at combating inflation brought on by spiraling oil prices and other factors.

In a move that markets widely anticipated, the central bank's Federal Open Market Committee voted 12-0 to increase its key interest rate by a quarter percentage point, or 25 basis points. The move brought the overnight funds rate to a target range of 3.75%-4%. [...] Updated projections the committee released Wednesday showed that a strong majority of officials think another hike is possible later this year.

The dot-plot grid of individual officials' expectations indicated that 16 of the 18 participants – Warsh has chosen not to submit a dot since taking the position – expected another rate increase, with four of those seeing two more as possible. Two participants expected the committee to stop at one hike. [...] "All three of those things lend themselves to a firm unanimous decision today," he said.

Despite a raft of conflicting recent statements from policymakers, markets had priced in a better than 90% chance that the FOMC would approve the increase, though there was chatter about the possibility of multiple dissents.

Persistently high inflation readings coupled with statements from Warsh a few weeks ago had convinced Wall Street that the Fed would OK its first rate increase since July 2023.

   The eight scheduled 2026 FOMC meetings are January 27–28; March 17–18; April 28–29; June 16–17; July 28–29; September 15–16; October 27–28; and December 8–9. The March, June, September, and December meetings include the Summary of Economic Projections (SEP).

### What time does the FOMC announce its decision? [...] The Federal Open Market Committee is the Federal Reserve body responsible for open market operations and the target range for the federal funds rate.

### Which 2026 FOMC meetings include the dot plot?

The March, June, September, and December 2026 meetings include the Summary of Economic Projections and its federal funds rate projections, commonly called the dot plot.

### How can an FOMC decision affect borrowing costs? [...] The FOMC directly sets the target range for the federal funds rate, not consumer loan rates. Its decisions and guidance can still influence Treasury yields, bank funding costs, mortgage rates, savings rates, and other borrowing costs, but those rates do not always move one-for-one with the Fed.
